meta.note: DEMO crop perishability profiles — evidence-informed shelf-life ranges for storage-risk awareness. Production would source from ICAR/NHM cold-chain guidelines or verified post-harvest research. All numeric ranges are approximate and educational, not predictive.
meta.purpose: Enables crop-aware storage-risk analysis so the system can warn when planned storage duration may exceed supported shelf life

profiles.storageConditions: Cool, dry, well-ventilated. Ambient storage 10-15°C ideal. Avoid moisture and direct sunlight.
profiles.riskNotes: Onion stores relatively well. Risk increases if bulbs are cured improperly or exposed to high humidity (>65% RH). Sprouting begins after several weeks at ambient temperature.
profiles.sourceReference: Post-harvest handling of onion — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: 12-15°C, 90-95% RH. Do not refrigerate below 10°C (causes chilling injury). Handle gently to avoid bruising.
profiles.riskNotes: Tomato is highly perishable. Ripening accelerates at ambient temperature. Cold-chain integrity is critical. Each day of delay after harvest increases spoilage risk significantly.
profiles.sourceReference: Post-harvest vegetable storage — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: Dry grain at <12% moisture. Cool, dry storage. Sealed containers preferred. Fumigation may be needed for insect control.
profiles.riskNotes: Soybean is a durable grain when properly dried. Primary risks are moisture re-absorption and insect infestation, not rapid perishability. Long storage is feasible.
profiles.sourceReference: Grain storage principles — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: Dry grain at <14% moisture. Airtight containers preferred. Neem leaves or alum as natural protectants.
profiles.riskNotes: Rice is a durable grain. Moisture and insects are the primary threats. Properly dried rice stores well for months.
profiles.sourceReference: Grain storage principles — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: Dry grain at <13% moisture. Cool, dry storage. Airtight containers for extended storage.
profiles.riskNotes: Maize stores well when dried properly. Susceptible to weevil and aflatoxin if moisture is high.
profiles.sourceReference: Grain storage principles — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: Dry, clean storage. Moisture content <8% for lint. Cool, well-ventilated.
profiles.riskNotes: Cotton lint stores well. Primary risk is moisture absorption and contamination. Raw cotton is durable.
profiles.sourceReference: Cotton post-harvest handling — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)

profiles.storageConditions: Dry at <9% moisture. Cool, dry storage. Airtight containers to prevent aflatoxin development.
profiles.riskNotes: Groundnut is susceptible to aflatoxin contamination if stored with high moisture. Proper drying is critical.
profiles.sourceReference: Groundnut storage guidelines — general agricultural extension knowledge (demo approximation)
